gaps.explanation: 'What happened next' means 'the thing that happened'; 'that' cannot introduce the clause here because the sentence needs a subject inside it.

gaps.sentence: The lawyers, against ___ the case was brought, denied everything.
gaps.hint: the case was brought against them
gaps.explanation: 'Against whom' is the formal relative pattern; 'who' and 'that' cannot follow prepositions.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ hand in their essays late will lose marks.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to the students performing the action; the verb 'will lose' follows later in the sentence.

gaps.sentence: The police have arrested the man ___ stole the painting.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' is the subject relative pronoun for people in defining clauses.

gaps.sentence: It was the best meal ___ I have ever eaten.
gaps.hint: after a superlative, this pronoun is preferred
gaps.explanation: After superlatives ('the best ...'), 'that' is the preferred relative pronoun in defining clauses.
'What caused the fire' means 'the thing that caused it'; 'that' cannot act as the subject of this nominal clause.

gaps.sentence: There are times ___ I really miss my home town.
gaps.explanation: 'There are times when ...' is a standard pattern; 'when' stands for 'at which'.

gaps.sentence: He passed all his exams first time, ___ surprised everyone.
gaps.hint: refers to the whole previous clause
gaps.explanation: 'Which' can refer to a whole idea ('he passed first time'); this non-defining use never takes 'that'.
